paper_summary: This paper documents the conservation and restoration of a polychrome (painted) wooden coffin from the Dahshur archaeological area, Egypt, dating to the Late Period. It covers documentation, wood identification (Faidherbia albida), insect/microbial sterilization with nanochitosan, mechanical and chemical cleaning, reattachment of gesso layers with Paraloid B72, and consolidation of the painted layer with calcium oxide nanoparticles in Klucel G. Glass microballoons mixed with Paraloid B72 and earth pigments were used only as a gap-filling paste for the edges of the ground layer.
